n: Mormon pauses to explain the legal system: under Mosiah’s law, judges were paid according to the time they spent hearing cases.

f.w: receive wages according to the time
f.g: Unlike unpaid church leaders, civil judges were compensated — which, as verse 20 shows, could be abused.

n: Debt cases: an unpaid creditor could complain to a judge, who sent officers to bring in the debtor. If found liable, the debtor had to pay, lose his property, or be expelled as a thief.

f.g: Have his property taken to cover the debt.

n: A judge earned one senine of gold or one senum of silver per day, by law.

f.g: The basic gold unit — one day’s wage for a judge.

n: Mormon lists Nephite measures of gold and silver. The Nephites didn’t use Jewish units; they adjusted their system over generations until Mosiah standardized it.

f.w: they did not reckon after the manner of the Jews
f.g: These were standardized weights of metal used for exchange; scripture does not describe coins.

n: The four gold units, smallest to largest: senine, seon, shum, and limnah.

f.g: The largest gold unit; worth seven senines (1 + 2 + 4).

n: The four matching silver units: senum, amnor, ezrom, and onti.

f.g: The largest silver unit; worth seven senums.

n: A senum of silver equaled a senine of gold, and either would buy a measure of barley or other grain — anchoring the system to food.

f.g: Grain as a value standard — a day’s pay bought a day’s staple.

n: A seon of gold was worth two senines.

f.g: Worth 2 senines.

n: A shum was worth two seons — four senines.

f.g: Worth 4 senines.

n: A limnah equaled all three of the smaller gold units added together — seven senines.

f.g: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 senines. The doubling pattern made exchange simple.

n: An amnor of silver equaled two senums.

f.g: Worth 2 senums.

n: An ezrom equaled four senums.

f.g: Worth 4 senums.

n: An onti equaled all the smaller silver units combined — seven senums. Zeezrom will soon offer Amulek six of these.

f.g: Worth 7 senums — a week’s wage for a judge.

n: Mormon now lists smaller fractional units.

f.g: Smaller fractions for everyday purchases.

n: A shiblon was half a senum and bought half a measure of barley.

f.g: Half a senum. Alma later names a son Shiblon.

n: A shiblum was half a shiblon.

f.g: A quarter of a senum.

n: A leah was half a shiblum — the smallest unit.

f.g: An eighth of a senum.

n: This was their system of reckoning.

f.g: Counting or calculating value.

n: An antion of gold equaled three shiblons — a gold unit worth a senum and a half.

f.g: 1½ senums’ worth of gold.

n: The point of the digression: lawyers and judges were paid by caseload, so they stirred up riots and disputes to get more work — including turning people against Alma and Amulek.

f.w: for the sole purpose to get gain

f.g: Lawsuits, legal cases.

n: Zeezrom, skilled in the devil’s tactics, asks Amulek to answer some questions.

f.w: expert in the devices of the devil

n: Amulek agrees — but only to say what the Spirit allows. Zeezrom then offers six onties of silver (about six weeks of a judge’s pay) if Amulek will deny that God exists.

f.g: 42 senums — a large bribe.
God.

n: Amulek rebukes him: why tempt me? The righteous don’t yield to such bribes.
Amulek exposes Zeezrom: you know there is a God, but you love money more.

f.g: Money, gain.

n: He reveals Zeezrom never intended to pay — he only wanted Amulek to deny God so he could destroy him. Such evil will bring its own consequences.
Zeezrom switches tactics: you say there is a true and living God?
Amulek affirms it plainly.

f.g: Amulek answers briefly and directly, giving no opening for a trap.

n: Zeezrom asks: is there more than one God?

f.g: Zeezrom hopes to set up a contradiction once Amulek speaks of the Son of God.

n: Amulek answers no. In context — see verse 44 — he means the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit together are one Eternal God, united in purpose. Latter-day Saints understand the Godhead as three distinct beings who are perfectly one.
How do you know these things?

f.g: A test of Amulek’s authority.

n: Amulek answers simply: an angel told him.

f.w: An angel hath made them known unto me

n: Zeezrom asks whether the one who is to come is the Son of God.

f.w: Who is he that shall come

n: Amulek says yes.

f.g: Amulek testifies that the coming Messiah is the Son of God.

n: Will Christ save people in their sins? No, Amulek says — God cannot deny his own word. Christ saves people from sin, not in it.

f.w: save his people in their sins

n: Zeezrom twists this to the crowd: Amulek says one God, then a Son of God, and claims God won’t save — as if he could command God.

f.w: as though he had authority to command God
f.g: A typical lawyer’s distortion of an opponent’s words.

n: Amulek calls out the misrepresentation.

f.g: Amulek refuses to let his words be twisted.

n: He explains: God has said no unclean thing can enter heaven. Since salvation means entering heaven, no one can be saved while still in their sins.

f.w: no unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of heaven

n: Zeezrom asks: is the Son of God the very Eternal Father?

f.g: A title for Christ as Creator and as the Father of all who are spiritually reborn through him.

n: Amulek says yes: Christ is the Eternal Father of heaven and earth and everything in them — their Creator — the beginning and the end.

f.w: the very Eternal Father of heaven and of earth

n: He will come to redeem his people, taking on himself the sins of those who believe. They will have eternal life, and salvation comes no other way.
The wicked remain as if no redemption had been made, except for resurrection. All will rise and be judged by their works.

f.w: the loosing of the bands of death

n: Temporal (physical) death will be overcome by Christ’s death; everyone will be resurrected.

f.g: The death of the physical body.

n: In the resurrection, spirit and body reunite in perfect form, every limb and joint restored. We will stand before God with full memory — including a bright recollection of guilt.

f.w: a bright recollection of all our guilt

n: Resurrection comes to everyone — young and old, slave and free, men and women, wicked and righteous — not even a hair lost. All will face judgment before Christ, the Father, and the Holy Spirit, one Eternal God.

f.w: not so much as a hair of their heads be lost

n: The resurrected body is immortal: spirit and body joined forever, never to die or decay again.

f.g: Decay.

n: The people are astonished, and Zeezrom begins to tremble — the start of his change of heart. Mormon notes this is all he recorded of Amulek’s words.
